title: Round-up savings: spare change, on purpose
description: The piggy bank used to fill itself with whatever coins a pocket surrendered. Round-up savings is the digital version: every purchase rounds up to the next pound or dollar, and the difference quietly moves into savings.

body.heading: Small change, serious totals
paragraphs: A coffee at 3.60 rounds to 4.00 and saves 0.40. Trivial once — but a household makes hundreds of small purchases a month, and the round-ups typically gather into a sum that surprises people at year's end.
The trick works because the amounts sit below the pain threshold. Nobody budgets around forty pence; everybody benefits when forty pences gather somewhere useful instead of evaporating.

body.heading: Do it with or without an app
paragraphs: Many banks and savings apps offer automatic round-ups into a separate pot. Without one, the cash version still works: empty your pockets into the piggy bank nightly, and sweep notes' worth of coins into a real account monthly so the habit has a total.
One caution: round-ups are a savings starter, not a savings plan. Once the pot proves the habit, graduate to a fixed amount on payday as well — the spare change opened the door; walk through it.

takeaway: Round every purchase up and sweep the difference into savings: painless forty-pence pieces gather into real money — then graduate to a fixed payday amount too.
